meta.title: Claude Fable 5.1 vs OpenAI o3: Which one to choose in 2026? (models, context & API pricing & code compared)
meta.description: Compare Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI o3 architectural trade-offs, context windows, model APIs, and integration, and review side-by-side TypeScript to choose the right stack.

verdict: Choose Claude Fable 5.1 when you need a very large 1M-token context, up to 128K output, and predictable per-token API pricing, and when prompt caching matters, since cache reads are documented at $0.25 per million tokens. Consider OpenAI o3 when you want a reasoning-focused model and are evaluating it against published benchmarks and the OpenAI platform. Because specifications, benchmark scores, latency, and prices are version- and date-sensitive, confirm the current values against each provider's official documentation before committing.

comparison.category: Context window and maximum output. This criterion measures how much material a model can hold in a single request and how long a response can be, which drives whether a workflow needs chunking or retrieval workarounds.
comparison.toolA: Claude Fable 5.1 has a documented 1M-token context window and a 128K maximum output, per Anthropic's model overview. That combination is useful for long-document analysis, large codebases, and multi-step generation where the answer itself is lengthy.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 is a reasoning model, and its context window and maximum output should be verified against OpenAI's current model documentation, since limits can vary by model version and access tier. Treat any specific figure you see in third-party summaries as needing confirmation rather than as a fixed property.

comparison.category: Benchmark performance. This criterion looks at published results on standard evaluations such as MMLU and HumanEval, while acknowledging that scores are not directly comparable across providers unless the same version, prompting setup, and evaluation harness are used.
comparison.toolA: Anthropic publishes capability information for Claude Fable 5.1 in its official model documentation, and any benchmark figures should be read from that source and from Anthropic's release materials for the exact version. Avoid mixing scores from different model revisions or from third-party runs with different settings.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI publishes evaluation results for o3 in its official model and system documentation, and those results should be read from OpenAI's own materials for the specific version you intend to use. Because reasoning models can behave differently under different reasoning-effort or prompting settings, confirm the configuration behind any published score.

comparison.category: API pricing per million tokens. This criterion compares documented input and output token prices, plus prompt-cache pricing where available, since cost per task depends heavily on the input-to-output ratio and on cache reuse.
comparison.toolA: Anthropic documents Claude Fable 5.1 at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with prompt-cache reads at $0.25 per million tokens, which is 97.5% below the base input price. These are current documented figures and may change, so check Anthropic's pricing page before budgeting.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 pricing varies by model version and access tier, so the authoritative figures should be taken from OpenAI's official pricing page at the time you build your cost model. Rather than relying on a static number, compare your expected input and output volumes against the current published rates.

comparison.category: Latency and throughput. This criterion considers responsiveness in interactive and batch settings, noting that real latency depends on prompt size, output length, reasoning settings, region, and load rather than on the model alone.
comparison.toolA: Latency for Claude Fable 5.1 depends on factors such as context length, output length, and the serving configuration available to your account, so measure it with your own representative prompts. Anthropic's documentation is the right place to confirm current throughput and rate-limit details for your plan.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 is a reasoning-oriented model, and reasoning models often take longer to produce a final answer because they may spend additional computation before responding. Actual latency should be measured against your own workloads and verified against OpenAI's current documentation for the version and settings you use.

comparison.category: Model access and open versus closed availability. This criterion covers how developers obtain access, whether the model is served as a hosted closed model or released with open weights, and what that means for deployment flexibility.
comparison.toolA: Claude Fable 5.1 is documented as an Anthropic model accessed through Anthropic's platform and API, which means availability depends on account access and the provider's terms. Confirm current access requirements, regions, and any enterprise options on Anthropic's official documentation.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 is accessed through OpenAI's platform and API under OpenAI's terms, and access can depend on account tier and the rollout status of the specific version. Verify availability, rate limits, and any regional restrictions in OpenAI's official documentation before designing a dependency on it.

comparison.category: Prompt caching and cost optimization. This criterion evaluates levers for reducing repeated-input costs, which matters for applications that resend long system prompts, documents, or code context on every call.
comparison.toolA: Anthropic documents prompt-cache reads for Claude Fable 5.1 at $0.25 per million tokens, 97.5% below the $10 per million base input price, which can meaningfully reduce cost for workloads with stable prefixes. Cache behavior and eligibility should be confirmed in Anthropic's pricing and prompting documentation.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI offers caching-related features on its platform, but whether and how they apply to o3 depends on the current API version and documentation. Check OpenAI's official pricing and API docs to see which caching options are available for the specific o3 version you plan to use.

comparison.category: Practical use cases. This criterion maps model strengths to real workflows, recognizing that fit depends on the task, the amount of context required, the acceptable latency, and the cost profile.
comparison.toolA: Claude Fable 5.1 suits long-context work such as analyzing large document sets, summarizing extensive codebases, and generating substantial outputs up to 128K tokens in one request. Its documented cache-read pricing also makes it a reasonable candidate for applications that repeatedly send the same large prefix.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 is positioned as a reasoning model and is often considered for tasks that benefit from extended deliberation, such as complex problem solving and multi-step analysis, subject to your latency budget. Confirm which tasks your evaluation supports before standardizing on it, since reasoning models can behave differently across settings.

comparison.category: API integration and developer experience. This criterion compares how straightforward it is to call each model, including SDK maturity, documentation clarity, and how much configuration the typical request requires.
comparison.toolA: Claude Fable 5.1 is called through Anthropic's API, with an official SDK and documented request parameters for model selection, token limits, and system prompts. The exact model identifier and current parameters should be taken from Anthropic's model overview before you ship code.
comparison.toolB: OpenAI o3 is called through OpenAI's API, which has a widely used SDK and documented parameters, though reasoning models may expose version-specific options that you should confirm in the docs. Verify the current model name and supported parameters for o3 in OpenAI's official documentation.

comparison.category: Verified Claude Fable 5.1 specifications and pricing
comparison.toolA: Anthropic documents a 1M-token context window, up to 128K output tokens, and API rates of $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens for Claude Fable 5.1. Prompt-cache reads cost $0.25 per million tokens, 97.5% below the base input rate; verify current pricing before deployment.
comparison.toolB: Context limits, maximum output, and pricing for this option depend on its model, provider, and service terms. Do not transfer Claude specifications to it; check the provider's current official documentation before deployment.

faq.q: Which model should I choose for a project that needs to process very long documents?
faq.a: Claude Fable 5.1 is the stronger fit on paper for this specific need because Anthropic documents a 1M-token context window and up to 128K of output. OpenAI o3's context limits should be verified against OpenAI's current documentation before you assume it can hold the same volume. If your documents fit comfortably within o3's documented limits, evaluate both on answer quality for your task.

faq.q: How does pricing compare between Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI o3?
faq.a: Anthropic documents Claude Fable 5.1 at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with prompt-cache reads at $0.25 per million tokens, 97.5% below the base input price. For OpenAI o3, read the current rates from OpenAI's official pricing page, since pricing varies by version and access tier and changes over time. Build your cost estimate from your own input and output token mix rather than from headline numbers alone.

faq.q: Can I rely on published MMLU or HumanEval scores to pick between these models?
faq.a: Published benchmark results are useful directional signals but are not a substitute for testing on your own data. Scores are only comparable when the same model version, prompting setup, and evaluation harness are used, and reasoning-model behavior can shift with settings such as reasoning effort. Read figures from each provider's official release materials and confirm the configuration behind them.

faq.q: Is latency a reason to prefer one model over the other?
faq.a: Latency depends heavily on prompt size, output length, region, load, and model settings, so it should be measured with your own representative requests. Reasoning-oriented models such as OpenAI o3 can take longer because they may spend extra computation before answering, while Claude Fable 5.1 latency will vary with context and output length. Check each provider's current documentation for rate limits and performance characteristics.

faq.q: Are these models open source, and does that matter for deployment?
faq.a: Both Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI o3 are documented as hosted models accessed through their respective provider APIs, so availability depends on account access and provider terms. That matters if you need on-premises deployment, strict data-residency guarantees, or the ability to run the model without a vendor dependency. Review each provider's official documentation and terms for the deployment and security options that apply to you.

faq.q: What about prompt caching and cost optimization?
faq.a: Anthropic documents prompt-cache reads for Claude Fable 5.1 at $0.25 per million tokens, well below the base input price, which helps when you resend the same long prefix. OpenAI's caching options for o3 should be confirmed in OpenAI's current API and pricing documentation, since feature availability can differ by model version. Map these features to your actual prompt structure before assuming savings.

faq.q: How do I get started integrating each model in code?
faq.a: For Claude Fable 5.1, use Anthropic's official client and the documented model identifier from Anthropic's model overview, then send a messages request with a model, max tokens, and message list. For OpenAI o3, use OpenAI's official client with the current o3 model name and verify supported parameters in OpenAI's documentation, since reasoning models may require different settings. Confirm both model identifiers against the providers' current docs before deploying.

faq.q: What are the main limitations I should keep in mind?
faq.a: Every specification in this comparison, including context limits, prices, benchmark results, and latency, is version- and date-sensitive and should be verified against the provider's official documentation before you commit. Benchmark numbers are not directly comparable across providers unless the same version and evaluation setup are used. Neither model should be treated as guaranteed to meet a specific quality or performance threshold without your own evaluation on representative tasks.
